newsitem.title: UK: UK food retailers firm in falling market. [CORRECTED 12:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK food retailers firm in falling market. [CORRECTED 12:23 GMT]

text.p: Shares in UK food retailers were steady or firmer in a generally weak market on Tuesday, helped by catch-up buying after recent underperformance and a buy note on Tesco Plc from Kleinwort Benson, traders said.

Tesco was up 1-1/2p at 302p, Asda Group was unchanged at 102-1/2p, Safeway Plc was up 2-1/2p at 327p and Sainsbury Plc was up 3-1/2p at 373p by 1128 GMT. The overall market was down 0.28 percent at the time.
"We've seen some defensive buying in the sector on its recent underperformance...all four were due a bit of a bounce," one marketmaker said.
Traders said food retail stocks had been given a boost by a "buy" note on Tesco from Kleinwort Benson.
Kleinwort analyst Simon Dunn said the brokerage had rated Tesco a "buy" for some time but the latest buy note came after a review of the company's interim results released last week.

"Tesco is at a discount to the market and momentum is not slowing...all the major food retailers except Sainsbury look cheap to us," Dunn said. (Corrects from "..all four food retailers.." to "..all the major food retailers except Sainsbury..")

Dunn said the companies should also be helped by the recent revival in forecourt petrol prices. Food retail stocks came under pressure this year on investor worries about a hefty price war over petrol.
"The bottom line is that petrol was sold at a loss in the first half and we may see a break-even or better on sales in the second half," Dunn said.
